label: no
controls_available: Difficulty 5 uses 5 fibres, 11 segments per fibre, 3 missing joins, 3 false joins, 13 slice positions, and crossing density 0.79.

Full mode provides wheel scrolling on linked slice canvases, drag orbiting on empty mesh, mesh-node drag merges, and slice-node clicks for red and green split seeds; CUT BETWEEN SEEDS and CERTIFY REPAIRED BRANCH are visible controls.
The configured runtime allows 180 seconds, with observation_window_ms 0 and frames_per_observation 1.
autonomous_processes: None in the Branch Repair task state. Generated nodes, initial edges, slice focus, camera angles, and seeds are initialized once and do not evolve without input.
The shared clock supplies timer and animation-frame infrastructure, but Branch Repair registers no timer, interval, requestAnimationFrame loop, physics step, or input-independent state update.
grouped_control_modes: Full linked-plane inspection via slice-canvas wheel scrolling.
Full mesh orbit via dragging empty mesh space.
Full mesh-node drag merge, which adds a missing edge.
Full slice-node seed placement, with red and green seed selection, which prepares a split.
Full CUT BETWEEN SEEDS, which removes a false edge.
Full CERTIFY REPAIRED BRANCH submission, which is administrative.

clause_i.reason: There is no common temporally delayed decision for an observation-free policy to fail against. The seed-dependent choices are ordinary static spatial topology choices, not choices induced by an autonomously changing task state.

clause_ii.reason: A current screenshot can expose the static linked slices, regenerated mesh, and visible controls needed for a normal screenshot-only spatial repair; the configured one-frame, zero-length observation bound is sufficient for that static information. This does not provide temporal prediction.

clause_iii.reason: After any H_t with no new action, the Branch Repair model remains unchanged: focus changes only in changeSlice, merges and splits only in pointer/click handlers, and orbit only in pointer handlers. No non-clock task-state evolution occurs for any 0 < tau < Delta, so no available merge, seed, cut, or certification action becomes unavailable or strictly less effective during a delay.

common_visible_process: None. The visible process consists only of synchronous redraws caused by wheel, pointer, and click input; the branch stylesheet adds no autonomous animation. Therefore there is no visible temporal evidence in W_t^w that could predict a degrading action opportunity.

pre_run.reason: The mathematical definition already yields No because clause (iii) fails for every legitimate control mode, so the pre-run threshold cannot change the catalog label and no seed-rate probe is applicable.

source_evidence.claim: The exact level-5 profile has five fibres, eleven segments per fibre, three missing joins, three false joins, thirteen slices, and crossing density 0.79; full mode exposes scrolling, mesh orbit, mesh-node merges, and slice-node seeds; the runtime settings are 180 seconds, zero observation milliseconds, and one frame.
The generator selects the supplied control condition and materializes only static geometry/edit-count parameters for level 5; it has no time-dependent generator parameter.
Seeded generation creates fixed node positions, initial/true/missing/false edges, slice focus, and public state; the public state contains no evolving task clock or autonomous process.
Rendering initializes fixed focus, edges, camera, seeds, and inspection flags; slice changes synchronously recompute linked views and topology after wheel/control input.
Orbit, merge, seed, split, certification, mesh drag, slice wheel, and slice click behavior are all installed as direct event handlers; no autonomous callback is registered.
The Branch Repair stylesheet defines static layout, colors, responsive rules, and input states, with no animation or keyframe rule for the mechanic.
The shared browser loads the mechanic and invokes its render once for the fetched state; Branch Repair has no separate update loop in the shared dispatch path.
The shared clock only schedules and drains callbacks that a task registers, then exposes the clock API; Branch Repair registers none of those callbacks.
The grader replays a static initial edge set and synchronous event transcript, checks fixed topology and visible-input provenance, and has no elapsed-time or autonomous-state criterion.
The verifier only loads the exported result and calls the Branch Repair grader; it does not add a time-dependent check.
The solver performs explicit merge, post-edit inspection, seed/cut, and certification actions; its short waits are browser interaction settling, not task-state evolution.
